newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian call money firm amid kuna shortage.
newsitem.headline: Croatian call money firm amid kuna shortage.

text.p: The Croatian call money rate held firm at 8.0 percent on Tuesday after rising one percentage point on Monday amid a kuna shortage, money market dealers said.
No more than 14.6 million kuna ($2.3 million) had been settled by 0830 GMT, with another 15 million kuna sought by banking borrowers.

Their resources were depleted over the long bank holiday weekend. Monday's reserve payment also drained 3.52 billion kuna from the banking sector, or 91 million kuna more than a fortnight ago, due to a rise in deposits, the central bank said.
Banks' overall balances fell to 330 million kuna at the end of Monday. This left seven banks short of 17 million, which they bought in overnight trade on the money market.

They also borrowed 252.7 million kuna through a central bank Lombard facility, additionally increasing the outstanding loans to 294 million this morning, an official told Reuters. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075 ($ = 6.488 Croatian Kuna)
